summary: Revise the logs contract from the c2004 deployment evidence

delivery.outcome: Revise the v0.1 event contract into v0.2 against the 315-event c2004 deployment: an open namespaced eventType, source split from producer, subjectState split from outcome, a PLAN/APPLY mode, inputHash as self-evidence, and null instead of sentinel placeholders.
nonGoals: No change to the POA process registry, request grammar or propose-only boundary
No projection field map; the SODL/PLOG drift stays recorded as an open risk
No rotation or retention model; empty segments are already rejected by LOGS-STORE-EMPTY
No migration tooling for streams that were written without a hash chain
No docs/ or VERSION update; the budget caps this ticket at five implementation files, so they move to a dependent ticket

architecture.decision: Keep Protobuf canonical and keep the core vocabulary closed, but give a deployment its own namespace beside it. c2004 emitted three ticket.* types that no closed enum could hold, so eventType becomes a union of the reserved core enum and a namespaced pattern that may not squat 'logs.'. Absent optional values are null because c2004 wrote '-' on all 315 events, which made an unexecuted event indistinguishable from an executed one.
dataChanges: LogEvent gains source, mode, subjectState, inputHash and receiptRef
LogEvent.event_type becomes a string union; the EventType enum stays the reserved registry
evidence minItems relaxed from 1 to 0 because inputHash carries the binding
logs/control.jsonl re-projected into the v0.2 shape and extended to two chained events
architecture.rollback: Revert the branch. The contract version constant, the JSONL projection and the checker move together, so no stream written under v0.2 can be read by a v0.1 checker and no partial state survives a revert.

validation.evidence: LOGS-PASS over the two-event chained control stream
17 adversarial checks, including a positive case for a namespaced deployment type and a rejection of the '-' receipt placeholder
